exposure: Age groups: adolescents (10-19 years), early adulthood (20-24 years), advanced maternal age (35 years and above)
cohort: Adolescents (10-19 years old) and women aged 20-24 years and 35 years and above presenting in labor at QECH, Malawi
finding: While adolescents represented a significant proportion of pregnant women (20.4%) and were at higher risk for some complications like STIs, their neonatal outcomes were comparable to older groups, suggesting peripartum care as a potential factor.
